citations.assessment: The narrative names Onkelos bar Klonikos as Titus’s sister’s son and gives the consultation. This attests the kinship in the narrative. It leaves open whether the Torah translator is the same Onkelos.
The baraita attributes the cherub interpretation to Onkelos the convert and adds that they face like a student taking leave of his teacher.

The sugya gives Eliezer and Yehoshua as the transmitters of the Torah Targum and Yonatan as the transmitter of the Prophets. The voice stops disclosure of the Writings. The Ezra objection is answered by forgetting and re-establishing the tradition.
The scanned edition’s OCR gives year 3868 and attributes the teaching chain to Megillah. Heilprin’s locator 28 still needs edition collation.

citations.assessment: The direct Rashi gloss reads “it was forgotten” and then re-established, as against the local Heilprin reading “it was improved.” The translation now explicitly attributes each reading to its witness.

The relevant closing discussion preserves disagreement about using a commentary instead of Targum, cites the Sinaitic position and quotes the translation-and-addition baraita. It does not supply the Heilprin reading “was improved.”
The located passage has Hillel and Shammai withholding Torah instruction pending circumcision. The historical equation of Onkelos figures and the correspondence of עקל״א to this edition remain open.

The scanned Shalshelet makes Yonatan the one who saw Onkelos, reversing the direction of Heilprin’s wording. Megillah supplies the translation attributions, and the Zohar supplies the circumcision story.

Tosafot rejects deletion of the reading about translating, distinguishes Yonatan from the Writings Targum and places that Targum in the tannaitic period.

citations.assessment: Abarbanel lists Onkelos in the same generation as Gamliel II. The located introduction passage does not explicitly identify Onkelos as his student. The narrator’s nonfinding remains in the translation.
The named cook brings bread to Rabban Gamliel in the vessel-testing episode. The passage gives no elder/younger disambiguator.
The general rule names beds and articles of use. The Onkelos episode names Gamliel the elder and specifies the value of what he burned. Heilprin combines the detail with the surrounding rule.
The complete comparison calls the visitor Aquilas and gives the dialogue with Eliezer and Yehoshua. The source difference bears on the proposed identification.
The parallel calls the visitor Aquilas and likewise gives the two encounters. The speakers and naming are preserved separately.
The inheritance episode names Onkelos and the Dead Sea. The current digital paragraph is 6:12; Heilprin’s chapter 8 remains visible.

The named passage supplies the Eliphaz ibbur and explains that Eliphaz took silver and gold and spared Jacob. Heilprin summarizes this as taking all Jacob’s possessions. The underlying passage identifies this occurrence of G.N.
